projects.title: Context Atlas
projects.summary: A structured context system that connected product concepts, content rules, source authority, and retrieval requirements for an AI-assisted support experience.
projects.roleClaim: Led the content-system definition and facilitated implementation decisions with product and engineering.

projects.title: Evaluation Loop
projects.summary: An evaluation system for checking whether generated product content was grounded, structurally valid, and safe to publish.
projects.roleClaim: Designed the evaluation framework and worked with engineers to operationalize it.

projects.title: Localization Prototype
projects.summary: A prototype that transformed source content into structured locale-ready variants for review.
projects.roleClaim: Created the prototype and reduced localization preparation time.

claims.text: Mapped product concepts, user states, content rules, and source authority before designing retrieval.
Facilitated a shared semantic contract used by content, product, and engineering.
Improved retrieval consistency by making authority and state explicit.
Defined structural, grounding, safety, and language-quality evaluation dimensions.
Connected the evaluation schema to an automated test run and human review queue.
We implemented the evaluation pipeline across the product.
Reframed localization preparation as structured transformation rather than string replacement.
Built the production integration that generated locale-ready variants.
Reduced preparation from hours to minutes in the prototype workflow.

sourceReferences.excerpt: The team first mapped product concepts, user states, content rules, and source authority so retrieval could assemble the right context for each situation.
Each context object required a concept, state, authority, source reference, locale, and expiry rule.
Content, product, and engineering agreed on shared definitions and recorded ownership for each contract field.
The evaluation covered structural validity, grounding, safety constraints, and language quality before content reached human review.
The schema defined expected evidence, severity, automated checks, reviewer decisions, and failure recovery.
A structured test run produced repeatable results and routed uncertain cases to a human review queue.
The prototype transformed structured source content into locale-ready variants for review. The case study does not show the production integration or identify implementation ownership.
In the prepared example, the prototype reduced manual preparation from several hours to less than ten minutes.

capabilityLens.label: AI systems capability lens
capabilityLens.context: Investigate whether the reviewed work demonstrates the ability to understand complex context, contribute technical systems thinking, and execute across product, content, and engineering.

capabilities.label: Context understanding
capabilities.definition: Frames the problem, identifies relevant concepts and states, and connects decisions to source authority and user context.
observableSignals: Defines the operating context before proposing outputs
Connects user state, product state, and content behavior

capabilities.label: Technical depth
capabilities.definition: Translates content or product intent into schemas, system rules, integrations, evaluations, or implementation constraints.
observableSignals: Shows implemented or testable technical behavior

capabilities.label: Cross-functional execution
capabilities.definition: Moves work across disciplines through clear decisions, ownership, collaboration, and verifiable outcomes.
observableSignals: Creates decisions used by multiple functions

gaps.explanation: The evaluation project uses collective ownership language without showing which decisions or implementation steps the portfolio owner personally led.
The portfolio claims a production integration but provides only a prototype description and no implementation artifact.
Cross-functional execution is not described in the localization project material reviewed by Pheet.
The localization framing may transfer to AI systems work, but the reviewed artifact does not show how it handled model behavior, retrieval, or source authority.

interviewQuestions.question: Which parts of the evaluation pipeline did you personally define or implement, and which decisions belonged to other team members?
interviewQuestions.purpose: Clarify personal ownership within a collectively described project.

interviewQuestions.question: What moved the localization prototype into production, and what implementation artifact could show your contribution?
